steps.what: List open project needs and objectives already logged.
Coordinate or direct development, energy assessment, engineering, or construction activities.
Record the direction and the activities still open.

tasks.design: Open project needs and objectives are listed from {PROJECT}. The manager coordinates or directs the development, energy assessment, engineering, or construction activities. An activity with no id is not listed. The list does not direct the work, and the manager writes the direction record in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities sat in separate logs, so the clash showed up in the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The project record can list logged activities before the manager directs the work.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the activities meet the project needs is a judgement made in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The manager chooses what the team does next. A list of open items does not make that choice.
tasks.altitude: Direction of the work stays with the manager. The list only shows what is already logged.

reach.task: Direct construction activities on a site.
reach.learn: A logged activity is not an instruction to the crew.

evidence.claim: A project register can list open activities by type from records the company already holds. It does not direct the work.
EU AI Act Annex III 4(a) covers evaluation of workers. This list does not score who leads an activity. The manager directs.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: An activity id, a project id, and a date are required. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: The list contains only activities that already have an id on the project.
unknowns: Whether every development activity is logged before the direction meeting.
research_questions: Which activities are still agreed only in a call and never logged?

already_counted.description: Directing the activities and writing the direction record stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Check the activity list names the work the manager will direct.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes several activities have no id, so the manager rebuilds the list by hand and only logged rows are saved. High assumes the project record is complete before the meeting. The direction itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Manage project costs against the budget.

steps.what: Place wind project cost lines next to the budget limits.
Manage which wind project costs stay within budget limits.
Note the cost lines the manager will change.

tasks.design: Cost lines and budget limits already posted are placed side by side from {ERP}. The manager decides which wind project costs stay within those limits. A line with no budget id is not shown. The table does not cut a cost. The manager writes the note of what will change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost lines were copied into a second sheet before anyone could see the limit.
tasks.enabler_now: The ledger already holds the cost lines and the budget limits.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which cost to defer is a project decision, not a subtraction.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides which over-budget line moves and which one stands.

ambition.what: Which cost lines sit outside the budget in the week they are posted, rather than only at month end.

tasks.altitude: The manager still owns the budget decision. The table only shows posted lines against limits.

reach.task: Keep a construction budget inside its limit.
reach.learn: A variance row is not a decision to cut the work.

evidence.claim: A ledger can place each posted cost line next to its budget limit. It cannot decide which line to change.
A variance is a comparison of stored numbers. It is not an instruction to stop work.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: A cost line id, a budget id, and an amount are required. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Only posted amounts are compared. A missing amount is left blank.
unknowns: Whether every commitment is posted in the week it is made.
research_questions: Which costs are still agreed with a supplier and not yet on the ledger?

already_counted.description: Deciding which costs stay inside the budget, and noting the changes, stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Check each variance row uses the budget id the manager recognises.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes many cost lines have no budget id, so the manager matches them by hand. High assumes the ledger is complete and the table is ready. The choice of which cost to change is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List tax abatements, power purchase, land use, and interconnection agreements.
Lead or support negotiations involving those agreements.
File the points agreed and the points still open.

tasks.design: Current tax abatements, power purchase terms, land use terms, and interconnection agreements are listed from {DOCS}. The manager leads or supports the negotiations. An agreement with no id is not listed. The sheet does not concede a term. Personal details stay inside the negotiation file.
tasks.previous_blocker: The current terms were spread across mail, so the meeting started by hunting for them.
tasks.enabler_now: The agreement file can show the terms the company already holds.
tasks.still_hard: What to concede on tax, land, or interconnection is decided in the negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears the other side and decides which point to move.
tasks.altitude: The negotiation stays with the manager. The sheet only shows terms already on file.

reach.role: Property, Real Estate, and Community Association Managers
reach.learn: A stored term is the starting point, not the concession.

evidence.claim: An agreement file can show the current tax, power purchase, land, and interconnection terms. It does not negotiate.
Personal details of a landowner should stay limited to the terms of that agreement. GDPR data minimisation applies to that file.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: An agreement id and a term id are required. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: The sheet shows only terms stored on that agreement. It does not add a position.
The negotiation file is visible only to people who work on that agreement.
unknowns: Whether landowner contact details are stored on the agreement or in a separate list.
research_questions: Which negotiation points exist only in mail and not on the agreement record?

already_counted.description: Leading the negotiation and filing the open points stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Check the term sheet names only agreements that are still open.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes key terms are still only in mail, so the manager assembles them by hand. High assumes each open agreement has its terms stored. The negotiation itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assemble scope, tasks, resources, schedules, costs, and other project information.
Create wind energy plans, including goals and contingencies.
File the accepted plans as the project baseline.

tasks.design: Scope, tasks, resources, schedules, costs, and other project information already stored are assembled from {PROJECT}. The manager creates the wind energy plans, including the goals and the contingencies. The accepted version is filed in {DOCS} as the baseline. A row with no id is not assembled. The draft is not the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope, schedule, and cost lived in separate files, so the plan was retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Those records can be assembled into one draft the manager then completes.
tasks.still_hard: Goals and contingencies are the manager's judgement. They are not in the cost file.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sets what the project is trying to achieve and what risk it will carry.
tasks.altitude: The plan baseline is the version the manager accepted. The assembly does not set the goals.

reach.task: Set the baseline for an engineering project.
reach.learn: A filed plan is the accepted version, not the first assembly.

evidence.claim: A project record can assemble scope, schedule, resource, and cost rows the company already holds. It does not write the goals.
The baseline is the version a person accepted. An assembled draft is not that version.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: A scope id, a schedule id, and a cost id are required before a row is assembled. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Goals and contingencies are entered by the manager. They are not copied from the cost file.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the development manager.
unknowns: Whether contingencies are written on the plan or only discussed in the kickoff.
research_questions: Which plan sections are still free text with no source id?

already_counted.description: Writing the goals, the contingencies, and the acceptance of the plan stays with the manager.

incremental.description: Check the assembled rows still match the scope the manager intends to file.

approvals.approved_version: plan version and the schedule ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes scope and cost rows lack ids, so the manager assembles the plan by hand. High assumes those rows are complete and only goals and contingencies are written by the manager. Filing waits for acceptance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The development manager still directs the work, still decides which costs stay inside the budget, and still leads the negotiation. Records can be listed first. The manager still sets the goals and the contingencies on the plan.
reach: Construction managers supervise a site against a specification, and this job learns a listed activity is not the direction.
Architectural and engineering managers accept a design change before it is filed, and this job learns a project plan is filed only after the manager accepts that version.
skills_to_grow: Read a cost line against the budget limit before explaining a variance.
Write goals and contingencies that the schedule and the cost records do not contain.
Keep negotiation points and the direction of the work as the manager's own decision.
role.ambitious_version: Each wind project has one plan whose scope, schedule, and cost lines cite the records they came from, and the manager's goals and contingencies sit on that same version.
